1. The specific mechanical proposal

The proposed change is to give each field connection two physically different separation interfaces:

Ordinary interface: retract reusable bearing pins after individually observing their load return and separation.
Exceptional interface: remove the failed contact, its opposing counterhold and the attached member together, leaving the internal jam closed.
Restrained-rack operation: subsequently dissipate the captured internal energy while mechanically retaining the assembly.

The intended benefit is to stop making routine reconfiguration consume sacrificial wafers, while keeping an escape route that does not depend on a jammed ordinary connector becoming reversible.

That organization still uses substantial prior art. JAXA lists a resettable 10 kN release device with a 52 × 43 mm envelope, mass at most 350 g and a 20-operation life. US6450064B1 describes guided segments, rolling elements and a recessed rotating race. Neither supplies this frame’s shear, moment, controlled load return or industrial renewal life. Temporary load transfer and link replacement also appear in US8997873B2. I do not claim those mechanisms as new. 
Research and Development Directorate
+2

The potentially useful contribution would have been the complete repeatable operation across both interfaces, independent supports, stock and rack. This revision has not completed that contribution.

Ordinary connection

The current candidate uses:

Element	Introduced construction
Structural bearing pins	Two retained 12 mm half-pins
Pin actuation	Positively coupled 6 mm diameter, 1 mm lead screws; separate position and load observations
Withdrawal stroke	Approximately 11.3 mm into the respective cheeks
Actuation access	Two small permanent bevel boxes and a removable geared fork
Healthy joint admission	15 kN
Pin material	H1025-treated precipitation-hardening stainless steel
Pin design stress allowance	Introduced 500 MPa
Calculated hollow-pin stress screen	Approximately 452 MPa at the healthy admission load

The actuation screws do not receive the full structural shear load by assertion. The pin bodies and bearing cheeks carry it. The screws withdraw those pins only after the separate unloading operation.

The former rear cam was discarded because it intersected the backplate. Unfortunately, the replacement has its own concrete defect: its parked drive header at 420

title: Keep structural bearing separate from screw withdrawal
